lessonTitle: ▶ Unit 2 Concept Check — take this first
status: draft — items seeded toward the 27-item blueprint in docs/ap-physics-1-unit-2-architecture.md §10.3; not yet pilot-analysed (§10.5)
intro:
This is a short check of how you already think about **force and motion** — before the unit teaches it.

- It is **not graded** and does **not** affect anything.
- You will only be shown your **score and percentage**. You will **not** be told which questions you missed, or why — no item analysis is provided.
- You will take **this same check again at the end of the unit**, so you can see how much your thinking changed.
- No calculator, no equation sheet, no formulas — every question is answerable by reasoning. Answer every one; there is exactly one best answer.

The end-of-unit version shuffles the questions and the answer choices, so don't try to memorise positions.

items.stem: A puck is given one quick shove and then slides across frictionless ice at a steady speed. While it is sliding steadily, the horizontal forces on it are:
choices: a forward force, equal to the shove, that keeps it moving
a forward force that is slowly running out
zero — no horizontal force acts
a backward force only

items.stem: A spacecraft far from any star is coasting in a straight line with its engine switched off. Its velocity is:
choices: slowly decreasing, because there is no engine thrust
constant, because the net force on it is zero
constant only while some leftover thrust remains
increasing, because nothing opposes it

items.stem: A ball rolls across a level floor and gradually slows to a stop. The best explanation is:
choices: the 'force of motion' it was given gradually wears off
a friction force acts backward on the ball the whole time
gravity pulls it to a stop
moving objects naturally return to rest

items.stem: A book lies at rest on a level table. Which statement is correct?
choices: No forces act on the book, since it is not moving.
Only gravity acts on the book.
Gravity pulls down and the table pushes up; these balance.
The table pushes up; there is no downward force on a resting object.

items.stem: A picture frame hangs motionless on a wall from a nail. The number of forces acting on the frame is:
choices: zero — it is not moving
one — gravity
at least two — gravity, plus the support from the nail/wire, which balance
one — the support from the nail

items.stem: Two people push on a heavy crate from opposite sides: one pushes right with 300 N, the other pushes left with 250 N. The crate:
choices: does not move, because two people are pushing it
accelerates to the right, driven by a net force of 50 N
accelerates to the right, driven by a net force of 550 N
moves at constant speed to the right

items.stem: A box is pushed across a floor and moves at a perfectly constant velocity. About the horizontal forces on the box:
choices: the push is the only horizontal force
the push is larger than friction, which is why it moves
the push and friction are equal in size and opposite in direction
there is no friction, since the box keeps moving

items.stem: An astronaut takes a 2 kg rock from Earth to the Moon. On the Moon, compared with on Earth, the rock's mass and weight are:
choices: both smaller
both the same
same mass, smaller weight
smaller mass, same weight

items.stem: Which quantity is a measure of how hard it is to change an object's motion, and does not depend on where the object is?
choices: its weight
its mass
the gravitational force on it
its size

items.stem: The same net force is applied to a full shopping cart and to an identical empty one. Compared with the empty cart, the full cart's acceleration is:
choices: larger, because it has more mass to carry it forward
the same, because the net force is the same
smaller, because more mass means less acceleration for the same net force
zero, because it is too heavy to move

items.stem: Block X has twice the mass of block Y. Each experiences the same net force. Which block has the greater acceleration?
choices: block X (more mass)
block Y (less mass)
they have the same acceleration
cannot tell without the force value

items.stem: You push horizontally on a wall with your hand. The Newton's-third-law reaction to the force your hand exerts on the wall is:
choices: the wall pushing back on your hand
friction on your feet
your hand pushing harder to keep contact
your weight pressing down

items.stem: The Earth pulls down on a falling apple with a force of 1 N. The Newton's-third-law reaction to this force is:
choices: the air pushing up on the apple
the apple pulling up on the Earth with 1 N
the ground pushing up when the apple lands
there is no reaction while the apple is in the air

items.stem: A book rests on a table. Its weight (Earth pulling down) and the normal force (table pushing up) are equal and opposite. Are they a Newton's-third-law pair?
choices: Yes — they are equal and opposite
No — they act on the same object (the book) and are different types of force
Yes — every pair of balanced forces is a third-law pair
No — a third-law pair must be unequal

items.stem: A lamp hangs at rest from a cord. The cord's upward pull on the lamp and the lamp's weight are equal in size. The third-law partner of the cord's pull on the lamp is:
choices: the lamp's weight
the lamp pulling down on the cord
the ceiling holding the cord
there is no partner while the lamp hangs still

items.stem: A large truck collides head-on with a small car. During the collision, the force the truck exerts on the car compared with the force the car exerts on the truck is:
choices: larger, because the truck is more massive
equal in size
smaller, because the car is going slower afterward
larger, because the truck does more damage

items.stem: Two ice skaters, one heavy and one light, push off from each other. They push with equal and opposite forces. Immediately after, the lighter skater:
choices: moves off with the greater speed
moves off with the same speed as the heavier skater
moves off with the smaller speed
does not move, because the forces were equal

items.stem: A heavy box sits on the floor. You push horizontally on it, but it does not move. The friction force from the floor on the box is:
choices: zero, because the box is not sliding
equal in size to your push, in the opposite direction
always at its maximum value
in the same direction as your push

items.stem: A block slides across a rough table and slows to a stop. While it is sliding, the friction force on the block points:
choices: downward, opposing its weight
in the direction it is sliding
opposite to the direction it is sliding
there is no friction once an object is already moving

items.stem: A block sits on a ramp that is tilted at an angle. The normal force the ramp exerts on the block is:
choices: equal to the block's weight
greater than the block's weight
less than the block's weight
zero, because the ramp is tilted

items.stem: A ball on a string is whirled in a horizontal circle at constant speed. The net force on the ball points:
choices: forward, in the direction the ball is moving
outward, away from the centre
inward, toward the centre
there is no net force, since the speed is constant

items.stem: A car drives around a flat circular track at constant speed. On a free-body diagram of the car, you should draw:
choices: gravity, the normal force, and a separate 'centripetal force' toward the centre
gravity, the normal force, and friction — friction's net effect points toward the centre
gravity, the normal force, and an outward 'centrifugal force'
only a forward driving force

items.stem: A rocket is in deep space, far from any planet or air. It fires its engine. Can it accelerate?
choices: No — there is nothing for the exhaust to push against
No — engines only work inside an atmosphere
Yes — the rocket pushes exhaust backward, and the exhaust pushes the rocket forward
Only if it is already moving

items.stem: An elevator moves upward at a constant speed. The net force on a person standing inside it is:
choices: upward, in the direction of motion
zero
downward
upward, but decreasing

items.stem: Two balls, one twice as heavy as the other, are dropped from the same height at the same instant (ignore air resistance). They:
choices: land at the same time
the heavier one lands first
the lighter one lands first
the heavier one lands twice as fast

items.stem: A ball is thrown straight up. At the exact highest point of its path, its acceleration is:
choices: zero, because its velocity is momentarily zero
directed downward, with the same size as everywhere else in the flight
directed upward
changing direction at that instant

items.stem: A truck tows a trailer along a straight, level road at a steady 60 km/h. The forward pull of the truck on the trailer, compared with the total backward resistive force on the trailer, is:
choices: larger
equal
smaller
zero
